dossier.architecture: Station-fed elevator/arm with separate multipurpose ground collector and central donut climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; drive module specification not established in this interview.
subsystems.intake: Station funnel and infrared-triggered roller scorer; Froggy ground arm collects coral/algae, scores L1 and processor.
subsystems.transfer: Belted roller groups and treaded algae contact surfaces maintain control.
subsystems.scoring: Internally rigged elevator and pivoting arm; opposite-side motors counterbalance arm rather than simply minimizing motor height.
subsystems.endgame: Two hook pairs rotate against cage through changing leverage; hard stops and robot weight retain climb without a ratchet.
subsystems.controls: One driver/two human players; one-button nearest-face alignment, front/back scoring and retreat-before-stow collision protections.

versions: Reinforced pivot plates and added belt tensioning.
Cooling added to Limelights and radio after overheating. Build thread contains further version history beyond this interview summary.
dossier.analysis: The counterbalance and passive climb retention illustrate why a generic rule such as all motors must be low is insufficient. Evaluate complete torque and CG geometry, including the scoring-to-stow collision path.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.body:
# 2025-694: A dedicated low-task arm adds work without monopolizing the elevator

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The station funnel uses powered surfaces and an IR entry sensor. The separate Froggy mechanism acquires coral/algae from the floor and scores L1/processor; its source gives a 48:1 X60 pivot and 2:1 X60 roller drive. A linked shaft/chain keeps the side plates synchronized, while added angle reinforcement stiffens their weak direction.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team describes reinforcement after structural analysis and a software interlock that delays retracting Froggy until the chassis backs away from the reef. The main arm’s motor placement is also used for counterbalance.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Low-level work can justify a dedicated mechanism when it shortens cycles and releases the primary scorer for another role. That benefit is conditional on interference: two mechanisms must be able to store, acquire and move without colliding. A geometric safety interlock should therefore be part of the architecture reference. “Button released” is not sufficient evidence that an external mechanism can retract safely.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test concurrent main-arm/Froggy poses, compare complete L1/algae cycles, and verify retreat detection before retraction under localization error.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
